items.title: Bloch torsion isomorphism for Suslin zero-homology of an open subscheme with smooth projective compactification
items.difficulty_reason: H2: the proper Bloch theorem alone does not handle the boundary of an open scheme. The author separates codimension-at-least-two and divisorial boundaries, uses the double construction and compatible surface torsion diagrams for the characteristic-zero base, and then combines a smooth hyperplane section, compact-support pushforward and Albanese torsion functoriality to induct on dimension. Positive characteristic uses the earlier comparison through its precise prime-to-characteristic torsion scope. The boundary reduction and surface-to-higher-dimensional closure are an independent nonroutine H2 mechanism, while the cited proper Bloch and Roitman theorems remain inputs rather than being attributed to this proof or used to inflate H3.

compared.relation: Smooth projective modulus-versus-Suslin comparison, old4.5; none of the six new statements is this claim.
Neron-Severi lattice restriction rank, not a Suslin or motivic finiteness/comparison theorem.
LogarithmicTHH/TC projective-pair invariance of spectra, not zero-cycle relation comparisons.
Very-effective hermitian-K slice operation on homotopy groups, not top motivic cohomology finiteness.
Tensor ranks of alternating forms, not zero-cycle groups despite the generic paper title.
Multiplicative independence implies nonzero exterior product of field units, not open Bloch torsion.
Construction of a bielliptic-surface degeneration, not general normal-crossing relation descent.
Euler/Chow-Witt-to-Chow factorization on smooth affine varieties, not a zero-cycle relation comparison for these singular/projective pairs.

within_work_core_comparison: Producer H3 proposals3.5,5.4,6.2 are retained as H2 after reading their actual author proof burden. Advanced cited machinery and the paper's general subject do not confer H3.

Producer suppression of6.5 as a thin assembly is not adopted. Its relative-K nilpotent kernel divisibility at the surface base, Albanese torsion lifting of the kernel modulo m, projective-bundle embedding of a relation curve, and normal hyperplane induction give an independent H2 core beyond the smooth-pair modulus comparison2091.

Producer suppression of7.7 as subsumed by8.3 is not adopted. The actual7.7 proof extends a function on C union C_infinity over an affine complement, clears poles, perturbs a prescribed-base linear system while preserving restrictions, and rewrites the relation on two snc curves. This is not the point-blowup and all-strata hypersurface descent of8.3; sharing Bertini or being a prerequisite does not identify the proof cores.

Theorem8.4 and introductory1.6 assemble EKW with2091 and8.3; they are not additional IDs. Section6.3-6.4 finiteness consequences reuse6.2 with localization, resolution and divisibility, with no extra independent H2 count.

necessary_conditions.condition: algebraically closed base field of positive characteristic
k perfect and the irreducible components of D_red regular
k infinite perfect and X a normal crossing projective variety, in one of the two coefficient regimes
condition (star): the canonical map CH^LW_0(S_X) -> CH^BK_0(S_X) is an isomorphism
necessary_conditions.note: a genuinely conditional hypothesis, not a definition; the work lists only sufficient cases in lem:comparisonLWlci and calls the general question subtle at line 2624

necessary_conditions.condition: k algebraically closed, l a prime different from char(k), U admitting a smooth projective compactification
k finite, p-adic, or algebraically closed; m invertible in k; p not dividing m when k is p-adic
X integral, regular in codimension one, D effective Cartier; complete for parts (2) and (3) of Theorem 1.5

quantifier_and_regularity_points: Dimension restrictions are part of the statements and must not be normalized away: 1.2 and 1.6 allow d >= 0 (lines 227, 371), while 3.5 requires d >= 1 (line 1180) and 8.3 is stated for d >= 1 with induction starting at d <= 2 (lines 2697-2698, 2727).

The divisor in 1.1 and 3.5 is reduced effective Cartier (lines 211-212, 1180-1181); in 1.2 it need only be effective Cartier with regular reduced components (lines 1511-1512); 6.4 allows an arbitrary effective Cartier divisor (lines 2068-2069).

Coefficient regimes are not interchangeable: Z[1/p] when p > 1, and Z/m with m in k^x in characteristic zero (lines 375-377, 2871-2875). The restatement 4.5 writes R = [1/p] at line 1518 whereas the introduction writes Z[1/p] at line 233, a literal notational difference in the source.
Conditional dependence on resolution of singularities appears in the definition of Lambda (lines 493-494) and in the second half of the proof of 3.5 (lines 1228-1230).
The double S_X is formed for integral regular quasi-projective X and effective Cartier D (lines 821-825); later uses take X smooth projective and D reduced (lines 1115-1116).

The normalization and its projective normal compactification are fixed data in the definition of Suslin homology (lines 632-640); the remark that C_infty is treated as a reduced Cartier divisor at line 633 must be preserved.

In the reduction of 1.1(2) the specific plane curve is the one with homogeneous equation $x_0x^2_1-x^3_2 = 0$ (lines 1421-1423); the computation must keep this exact equation and the stated groups Omega_k + Z versus Z.

In the definition of the EKW group the two relation types are (c1) f in O^x_{C^N, nu^*(D)} with f(x) = 1 for all x in nu^*(D), and (c2) C an snc subcurve with f in O^x_{C, C cap D} (lines 2839-2846); both quantifiers are needed for the comparison.

The moving-lemma embedding-dimension inequalities in 8.3 are explicit numeric conditions: edim(C') = 2 < dim(Y'), edim(C' cap Y_i) + dim(C cap Y_i) <= 1 < dim(Y_i) for every other irreducible component, and the analogous inequality for components of D' (lines 2757-2765).
The degree of the alteration in 6.1 and 6.2 is a power of the exponential characteristic, and the resulting map h' is finite flat of that same degree (lines 1899-1901, 1965-1972, 2009-2010).

No limit process or completed object is introduced; the only 'limiting' step is the algebraic fact that a divisible torsion group of bounded exponent vanishes (lines 1225-1226), with bound exponent (d-1)! (lines 1209-1211).
core_recount_boundaries: In the introduction, 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.5 and 1.6 are announcement statements; their proofs appear later as 4.3 plus 4.4, 4.5, 5.4, 6.3-6.5, and 8.4. Announcements are not counted again as separate cores.
4.5 (thm:M1) is existing record 2091 and is not re-counted as a new candidate; the introduction statement 1.2 is likewise not counted.

6.3 and 6.4 are direct applications of 6.2 with localization sequences and of 1.2, so they are not separate cores. 6.5 is a comparison assembled by the same hypersurface induction used inside 4.1 and 8.3 and is not counted separately.
7.7 (snc-surface) is a genuine surface-only moving lemma, but its construction is generalized and subsumed by 8.3; counting both would double-count one geometric core, so only 8.3 is retained.

4.1 and 4.2 are supporting torsion statements with proofs inside the work; they feed 4.3 and are not independently retained because their mechanism is the double comparison already retained as 3.5 plus cited torsion theorems.

Cited results with no author proof are never counted: thm:suslinhomology (Schmidt), the motivic Hom identification in Section 2 (Kelly-Pedicchio), lem:LW-lci* (Krishna), and the items listed inside lem:comparisonLWlci.

Weak forms and direct corollaries are not split: cor:Main-8, remk:SS, the Russell Chow group consequences at lines 1493-1504, and the EKW presentation remark at lines 396-399 are applications, not new cores.

No candidate is proposed for the surface case of 8.3, for the d=2 seed in 5.4, or for the smooth projective finiteness lemma 6.1 taken alone; each is an input or a special case, not an independent second core.

source_notation_points.impact: could confuse which p is meant locally; the surrounding argument uses p only as the exponential characteristic

source_notation_points.literal_phenomenon: The theorem assumes 'the condition (eqn:star) holds' and then gives a parenthetical 'e.g., k is algebraically closed and D is reduced, or k is infinite and d <= 2'.

source_notation_points.literal_phenomenon: The proof says the case d <= 2 follows from Lemmas 7.1 and 7.4 'and in this case the result is unconditional'.
source_notation_points.impact: the unconditional base case does not discharge condition (star) for higher d; must be read as a claim about the base case only

Lambda in section3 means Z when k admits resolution of singularities and Z[1/p] otherwise. Preserve both the localized proof and the conditional integral branch; no unconditional integral positive-characteristic comparison.

Theorem5.4 is over an algebraically closed field and a smooth projective compactification of the open scheme; ell differs from char(k), with compactly supported etale cohomology. Do not add canonical/functorial conclusions beyond the stated isomorphism.

Section6 Lambda'=Z/m, m>=1 invertible in k and prime to the residue characteristic for a p-adic field. The singular finiteness theorem retains all three field classes, arbitrary projective schemes, and every i>=0.
Theorem6.5 has integral projective X regular in codimension one, U=X_reg, char(k)=0 and any nonzero integer m. It is neither an integral comparison nor a statement for arbitrary singular schemes.

Proposition7.7 concerns normal crossing surfaces over an infinite field in the paper's definition. Its snc relations require the stated componentwise smooth integral intersections, reduced pairwise intersections, and avoidance of triple intersections.

Theorem8.3 retains the perfect-field, reduced quasi-projective normal crossing setup, E=Y intersect closure of the other components, D=X_sing, and the exact source condition(8.1). Do not add projectivity to its statement merely because8.1 uses a smooth projective pair.
